issues.description: The lower telegraph wire set (starting at y=10.55 on the pole) runs backward to [poleX - 0.5, 9.5, -5.5 + iz * 0.4] where there is no post or structure, so 4 wires end floating in mid-air behind the house.
issues.fix: Either add a rear relay post cylinder at [9.3, 4.8, -5.5] (height 9.6, mat 'wood_dark') or route the second set of `k.tube` wires into an insulator rack mounted on the east side wall of the house.

issues.description: The east, west, and north exterior walls of the Victorian house are completely blank stucco boxes with zero windows, pilasters, or architectural detail (violating DESIGN.md's rule against blank flat walls).
issues.fix: Add recessed/framed windows with mullions, sills, and teal accent hoods on the west (`x = -8.2`), east (`x = 7.2`), and north (`z = -6.6`) façades across both storeys, plus vertical corner trim boards.

issues.description: The main roof is built from two stacked rectangular boxes (`size: [15.0, 1.5, 10.4]` and `[13.2, 1.3, 8.4]`), which reads like a stepped wedding cake / ziggurat rather than a Victorian gabled or mansard roof, and exterior windows lack mullions.
issues.fix: Add a decorative roof parapet/cresting rail or dormer windows to make the mansard roof look intentional, and add vertical/horizontal mullion bars (`size: [0.05, 1.75, 0.24]`, `mat: 'trim'`) to all exterior windows.

issues.description: The interior feels sparse in the center and along the north-east and south walls; the lead outreach desk at [0, 0, -4.0] looks tiny and isolated, and the paper stacks on desks are single plain white boxes (`size: [0.28, 0.14, 0.22]`) that look like bricks.
issues.fix: Frame the lead desk with a gated-outreach review counter or bookshelf/whiteboard on the north wall, replace single block paper stacks with 2-3 thin slightly rotated sheets (`height: 0.03`) plus `paper_stack` or `books` props, and add baseboards/wall wainscoting or a floor lamp near the interview corner.

keep: Front façade composition with the projecting Victorian bay wing, pyramid spire, covered porch with turned posts and railings, and stone path with mailbox
Telegraph pole with crossbars, teal ceramic insulators, and upper sagging wires connecting to the house eaves
Interior switchboard console on the north-west wall with its grid of brass/teal jack cylinders and looping patch cables
West wall pigeonhole mail-sorting cabinet with cubbies and letter bundles
Customer interview corner with two armchairs, round table, mug, and tall plant
